messages:
Ellen: Heads-up: we've been getting a steady stream of tiny GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1c since ~09:02. Looks different from the usual label-rollout pattern. :confused:
sched-bot: ALERT: eviction_rate[gpu-ap-southeast1c] = 4.6/min (10m avg).
Marco: Different how? nodeAffinity/taints still look normal?
Ellen: Yep. But noticed these pods request resources as \"requests: {\n  nvidia.com/gpu: \"0.25\"\n}\" via a custom device-plugin shim. Scheduler is treating them as 1 GPU due to our device-plugin reporting, so binpacking is off and many single-fraction pods are evicted when gang jobs land.
Rajat: Oof. We only support whole GPU counts in core scheduler assumptions; fractional device-plugins must advertise extended resources and we need a scheduler-compatibility layer. Any logs?
Ellen: Scheduler bind log: ```I0504 09:05:18.442 scheduler_predicate.go:210] Pod ml/feat-extract-18 failed predicate: requested 1 GPU but node free GPUs 0 (device-plugin reported integer counts)```
Olive: So the device-plugin is misreporting fractional allocations as integer capacities. Short-term: we should mark fractional pods as lower priority and increase warmpool for that AZ; long-term: update device-plugin + scheduler scoring to be fractional-aware.
Terry: Hotfix suggestion: add a mutating webhook that rewrites requests.nvidia.com/gpu fractional requests to annotations (e.g., "x.dev/fraction-gpu=") and converts requests to 0 for scheduler path while the plugin handles accounting. Ugly but buys time. Also consider a scheduler extender that reads plugin annotations to make placement decisions.
Marco: Before that, can we detect all pods using fractional gpu requests? Quick one-liner: ```kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests."nvidia.com/gpu"?!=null) | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests."nvidia.com/gpu" | contains(".")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) -> \(.spec.containers[].resources.requests)"'```
Ellen: Ran it: ~73 pods cluster-wide using fractional gpu requests, 48 in ap-southeast1c. Opening TICKET-5120: "fractional-device-plugin mismatch -> ap-southeast1c eviction wave" and assigning infra + runtime + device-plugin owners.
sched-bot: RUNBOOK: warmpool scale triggered by Marco at 2025-05-04T09:12:03Z: warmpool.prod-frac.ap-southeast1c 4 -> 12 (run id rp-5120a).
Rajat: Plan: (1) immediate warmpool bump + lower priority for fractional pods, (2) roll mutating webhook canary to annotate fractional requests and remove scheduler-visible gpu request, (3) update device-plugin to expose fractional allocs via extended resources or a scheduler-extender API, (4) add CI check to prevent non-supported fractional gpu requests without annotation.
Olive: I'll own the webhook PR canary to ml namespace at 10% traffic. Terry, can you prototype a scheduler-extender readme for how the plugin will surface fractional topology/packing constraints?
Terry: On it. Also note: NVLink topology constraints mean we shouldn't blindly pack fractional workloads across different GPU islands; extender should be topology-aware.
Ellen: Metrics after warmpool bump: eviction_rate 4.6 -> 1.0 in 11m. Keeping ticket open until device-plugin + scheduler changes land. Thanks all :thumbsup:
